sentences.span: the market is at a 68% probability of a hike, despite Warsh's hawkish tone that seemed to back him into the hiking corner
sentences.why: Every macro source from this window (TS Lombard, Mizuho, UBS, MUFG) frames the summer/early-Sept debate as being about a possible HIKE at the September FOMC, not a first cut. No source describes a summer-long cut debate; the sentence inverts the direction of the live policy debate.

sentences.span: US Treasury yields on Wednesday climbed back toward levels not seen since before the Global Financial Crisis, with the 10- and 30-year yields rising to 4.8% and 5.28% respectively
sentences.why: UBS explicitly frames the 10-year (4.8%, close to the 4.75% cited) as a pre-GFC level. Japan's 3%-since-1996 and the fourth-session global selloff to mid-2008 highs are separately confirmed in the Zerohedge/Goldman piece (15120: 'rose for a fourth straight session... climbing to 3.72%, the highest since mid-2008').

sentences.span: an investor who bought 10-year Treasuries at the yield peak of 4.99% in October 2023 would have earned a total return of more than 16% by now
sentences.why: DB frames the move as 'normalisation after the financial repression of the 2010s' (pre-2010 normal), and yield peak = price low, so 'bought at the late-2023 low' matches 'yield peak... in October 2023.' ~16% matches 'more than 16%.'

sentences.span: the AI investment boom is both the equity bull case and the duration bear case
sentences.why: Same article cites fiscal-risk premium/deficits ('governments apparently incapable of cutting spending'), energy-driven inflation, and AI capex/hyperscaler issuance crowding out sovereigns as the structural drivers keeping yields elevated.

sentences.span: the burden of proof has shifted from “why hike?” to “why not hike?”, meaning soft data now needs to stop the Fed
sentences.why: Mizuho's framing directly supports 'the event in front of the market is a live hike, not a pause' for the near-term window.

sentences.span: September is now close to 70% priced for a hike, with around 60bp total priced through mid-2027
sentences.why: Multiple sources (Mizuho ~70%, TS Lombard 68%, MUFG ~70%) describe the hike as priced at that probability, and Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole tone is documented across sources as the thing that could soften.

sentences.span: Domestic AI compute demand is likely to show an ~80% CAGR
sentences.why: Source is JPMorgan (per meta.json). Goldman's companion claim is separately confirmed in 15122: 'AI infrastructure: still the main driver of EPS growth.'

sentences.span: notable strength in ISG margins (15.0% v. GSe 11.7%)
sentences.why: Goldman's Callahan note; same passage states 'GIR remains BUY rated, raising EPS by ~38% overnight.' ISG (servers+storage) margin is labeled 'server margin' in the pulse, a minor simplification that doesn't change the figure or the call.

sentences.span: the rate on 10-year Japanese government notes touched 3% for the first time since 1996
sentences.why: The 3%/1996 fact is sourced, but no document frames a trade 'fading how far the BOJ actually goes' — sources instead describe rising BOJ hike expectations (roughly once/quarter, a September hike expected), the opposite of a fade thesis.

sentences.span: Despite sharply higher Treasury and JGB yields, neither currency has enjoyed sustained support, suggesting markets are demanding more than simply higher nominal returns
sentences.why: UBS explicitly says the classic yields-pull-money-home mechanism has broken down (USDJPY sits weak near 160 despite JGB yields at multi-decade highs), contradicting the sentence's claimed repatriation transmission.

sentences.span: actual oil exports from the Persian Gulf are 40% above the March trough on a rise of dark crossings
sentences.why: Transition sentence with no independently checkable claim beyond pointing at the export/flow data that the surrounding sourced content (Goldman GOAL note, Hormuz flow trackers) is actually built on.

sentences.span: actual oil exports from the Persian Gulf are 40% above the March trough on a rise of dark crossings
sentences.why: Source is Goldman Sachs (per meta.json); 'March trough' matches 'March low' and the 40% figure matches exactly.

sentences.span: anywhere from 2 million to 4 million barrels/day getting through versus the US administration's claim of 8m-10m b/d
sentences.why: The 2-4mb/d vs 8-10mb/d dispute is faithfully sourced (Bloomberg/Zerohedge). No document attributes single-day flow figures 'far above that' to JPMorgan; this appears to be an invented attribution to a named bank.

No source document contains a Long USO / XLE call from any desk. The only USO/XLE hits across the corpus are Goldman ETF authorized-participant disclosure boilerplate, not a trade recommendation. Per the voice contract, TRADE BOARD entries must be an explicit named-desk call; none exists here.

sentences.span: September screens as the worst performing month for the SPX followed by Q4 being the strongest quarter of the year
sentences.why: JPMorgan's own seasonality view says Q4 (which includes October) is the STRONGEST quarter, contradicting the claim that JPMorgan sees Sept+Oct as a soft stretch. Separately, the bond-index seasonality figure in 15120 says the index lost 'more than 1% on average in EACH of the two months' — i.e. >2% combined, not 'about 1% across those two months.'
